verification_report.summary:
All three propositions pass sequential verification relative to the expressly accepted foundations.

For ordered contact, the maximum potentials have positive bounded-product measures and converge uniformly, so locality and the compact-set weak-limit inequality apply. The frozen-neighborhood inequalities are patched for each fixed epsilon before taking epsilon to zero. Fixed truncations then give local total-variation convergence, including after restriction to the contact set. Increasing finite levels proves the extended-measure inequality without assuming finite total mass or subtracting infinite quantities.

For continuous obstacles, the quasi-everywhere obstacle bound becomes pointwise by the canonical-representative convention. The cited internal regularization theorem preserves the exact Hermitian background. Compactness of the decreasing superlevel sets makes the shifted smooth approximants admissible; the envelope property then gives uniform convergence and continuity. Competitor inclusion and translation by constants give the stated 1-Lipschitz bound.

For the unbounded-obstacle reduction, countable Choquet extraction gives one pluripolar exceptional set. Capping the obstacle above preserves both its envelope and contact set. Semipositivity makes the constant competitors and all truncations admissible. The bounded envelopes decrease to the genuine envelope by the quasi-everywhere competitor definition. For each fixed truncation level, bounded capacity convergence and uniform capacity control justify the limit against the fixed quasi-continuous coefficient. Its zero integral forces the measure to vanish on its positivity set. Locality and increasing exhaustion then prove contact support off the discarded poles.

The local bounded monotone-continuity input is corroborated by [Lemma A.2, Approximation of maximal plurisubharmonic functions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1804.02894); the nonclosed-background calculus is used as explicitly supplied. The third proposition remains conditional on bounded-obstacle contact support. No BMP, PVP, implicit bigness, or upper bound on total extended mass is used.
